title: perf(objectql): the cascade walk reuses the collection walk's dependents probe until its first write
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9USTJYAvMcxS7CFGZygeZG6)_

repo:objectstack#2 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmQAXHSQEgnYyx9tstb

Fixes #33699

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:级联删除时,引擎不再把第一个级联关系的子记录读两遍——收集阶段读到的结果在「删除走查」第一次写入之前直接复用。
- 为什么改:裁决 6893104201 的 c1 余项(行为中性的重复读合并);实测一条带 10 条明细的商机删除从 58 条 SQL 降到 57 条(SQLite 与 PostgreSQL 16 本地实测)。
- 风险与回滚:风险低。只在「收集后、走查首次写入前」复用,任何写入(级联子记录删除、set_null 清空)之后一律照旧现读;回滚即 revert 本 PR,无数据或协议变化。
- 先看:`packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-planning.ts`(walk 里取用与首次写入前的 forget 两处)、`packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-cascade.ts`(收集阶段保存探测结果)、`packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-delete-batch.test.ts` 末尾的 `[c1]` 三条钉子。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/engine-cascade-delete-batch.test.ts -t c1`,预期 3 条通过;读序列里 `line {"acct":"a1"}` 只出现一次。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

Ruling 6893104201 item c1: the cascade walk read the same child rows again. Measured on the M0 bench at `origin/main` e8cba8fe (SQLite, `--sql-log`, one warm delete of an opportunity with 10 line items), statements 22, 24 and 25 of the 58:

- 22 `select * from bench_line_item where opportunity = ?` — the collection walk's dependents probe (`collectCascadeDeleteSet`);
- 24 `select * from bench_line_item where id in (...)` — the recycle-bin snapshot (`RecycleBinCapture.onCollected`);
- 25 `select * from bench_line_item where opportunity = ?` — the deleting walk's probe (`walkReferencingRelations`), identical to 22.

Between 22 and 25 only reads run (the root snapshot and the child snapshot). So:

- `collectCascadeDeleteSet` keeps each probe's answer beside the set (a `WeakMap` keyed by the set, in `engine-delete-cascade.ts`), keyed by the referenced object, the relation and the exact ids asked.
- `walkReferencingRelations` takes the kept answer for a probe it repeats (`takeCollectedProbe`, one use each), and drops every kept answer right before its first write (`forgetCollectedProbes` before a `set_null` clear and before a relation's cascaded children are deleted). A cascaded child's delete or a clear runs hooks, and a hook may write a row the next probe must see, so every probe after the first write reads as before. A nested walk (grandchildren, a joining member) always runs after that point, so it always reads.

Two of the three reads merge, not three. The snapshot keeps its own read: it reads the rows raw through the driver, while the probe's rows come through the engine's `find()` (formula values computed, file references resolved, `afterFind` hooks applied, unselected declared columns answered as null). Handing the probe's rows to the snapshot would change what the recycle-bin entry stores and what a restore writes back, which a behaviour-neutral item cannot do. The PR says so in the `cascadeDeleteRelations` docblock.

Not touched: F1's batch shape, the five by-id fallbacks, ADR-0148 D1 (one snapshot read and one recycle-bin insert per root).

## Tests

- `packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-delete-batch.test.ts`, new top-level describe `[c1] the walk takes the collection's probe until its first write` (the file's existing harness):
  - every driver read of a cascade delete with two cascading relations, in order: the first relation's probe appears once, and the second relation, walked after the first relation's batch wrote, is read again as before. Driver reads 12 before, 11 after;
  - a row a child's `beforeDelete` hook writes after the collection is still found by the next relation's probe and deleted (by id, as the root of its own cascade);
  - the same after a `set_null` clear: a self-lookup `acct.parent` (`set_null`) is walked before `line`; the clear of `a2.parent` runs an `afterUpdate` hook that writes line `l9`, and the `line` probe that follows still finds it and deletes it (writes `deleteMany line l1,l2,l3`, `delete line l9`, `delete acct a1`; `a2.parent` is null).
- Existing pin that also guards the after-write rule: `recycle-bin/capture.test.ts` "a cascade dependent written after the set was collected keeps its own entry" (a grandchild written by a child's hook).
- One existing test changed, forced: `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/delete-record-predicate-walk-batched.integration.test.ts` pinned 6 reads of the master_detail relation for a 3-batch multi delete, because the collection walk and the deleting walk each read it. The deleting walk now takes the collection walk's answer, so the pin reads 3 (`detail: 3, link: 3, tags: 3`); its comment names ruling 6893104201 c1.

## Acceptance notes

- One fewer engine read means an `afterFind` hook on the child object is called for one system-identity read fewer per cascade. The only shipped `afterFind` hook (plugin-audit read audit) returns at once on a system read.
- Isolation: the walk's old re-read could also see a row another transaction committed between the collection and the walk. Such a row is now found only if a later probe reads it; the window in which a concurrent insert escapes the cascade was already open between the walk's probe and the root's DELETE, and it moves earlier by the length of the restrict judge and the snapshot read. Within one unit of work nothing changes.
- Not used as the guard: the engine's `writeEpoch` (it would also catch writes by other requests in this process, so reuse would rarely apply under write load, and read-audit flushes bump it at arbitrary times). The guard is this walk's own first write.
- Observation — dropped: the same predicate asked twice in one transaction, no wrong answer (see the closing comment on #34533, closed not planned). In the warm-delete capture of the SQLite `--sql-log` run above (statement list of one delete, after this PR), statements 25 and 26 are the predicate arm's read-door question for the line batch, asked twice in the same transaction in two shapes: 25 `select id from bench_line_item where ((id in (10 ids)) and (opportunity in (select id from bench_opportunity where account in (select id from bench_account)))) trx7`, 26 the same with `order by id asc limit ?` appended, `trx7`. The same pair appears once per delete in every one of the five deletes (raw log lines 4042/4043 trx3, 4101/4102 trx4, 4160/4161 trx5, 4222/4223 trx6, 4281/4282 trx7), and before this PR as statements 26 and 27. Correction to the earlier wording of this note: both statements DO carry the transaction tag (`trx7`, as the other cascade statements 22 to 33 do). My first statement list cut every line at 160 characters, which hid the tag; the raw `knex:query` log shows it. What remains is the second, ordered-and-limited asking of the same predicate. No wrong answer reproduced; call sites not traced.

## Verification

<details><summary>Bench, statement counts (my local runs, shared 4-core box)</summary>

`node packages/qa/dogfood/bench/sql-perf/bench.mjs --scale 100000 --only cascade_delete_opportunity --sql-log --cascade-deletes 5`, one opportunity with 10 line items per delete; first number cold, then warm:

| dialect | before (e8cba8fe objectql) | after (this branch) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| SQLite | 69, 58, 58, 58, 58 | 68, 57, 57, 57, 57 |
| PostgreSQL 16 (private cluster, fsync off) | 69, 58, 58, 58, 58 | 68, 57, 57, 57, 57 |

The SQLite statement lists of one warm delete, before and after, differ in exactly one line: statement 25 above. The PostgreSQL before leg ran base objectql sources built into this tree, so its result file is stamped with the branch commit; the build was confirmed free of `takeCollectedProbe` (`ablation-dist-preflight --absent`) and rebuilt at HEAD afterwards. Milliseconds are not reported: a `--sql-log` run carries the log's cost.
</details>

<details><summary>Suites and typecheck</summary>

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` at be88f869 (head: the relay's merge of `main` plus the set_null pin), under the verify lock: VERDICT command-exit 0, Test Files 605 passed (605), Tests 13512 passed (13512). At 2d58ed7e (the code commit) it was 605 / 13511.
- `src/engine-cascade-delete-batch.test.ts` alone at be88f869: Tests 18 passed (18). eslint over the test file: exit 0.
- `pnpm typecheck` in `packages/objectql` after a declaration build of its dependency closure: VERDICT command-exit 0; test layer 39 files / 233 errors held in `test-typecheck-debt.json`.
- eslint over the three touched source files: exit 0.
</details>

<details><summary>Ablations (each via scripts/ablation-replace.mjs, restored to the HEAD blob, git diff HEAD empty)</summary>

1. The walk never takes a kept probe (`takeCollectedProbe(...)` replaced by `undefined`): the read-order pin goes red, 12 driver reads where 11 are pinned.
2. No forget before a relation's cascaded children are deleted: 3 red — the read-order pin (the second relation is not read again), the hook-written-row pin (the late row survives), and the existing recycle-bin pin (the late grandchild survives).
3. No forget before a `set_null` clear (anchor `must see.` plus the `forgetCollectedProbes(cascadeSet);` line after it, 1 hit, replaced; blob 4170445f to ac3b3194), at be88f869: the new set_null pin goes red, line `l9` survives (`rowsOf('line')` returns `[{ id: 'l9', acct: 'a1', name: 'late' }]` where `[]` is pinned); Tests 1 failed, 17 passed (18). The other 17 stay green, so this forget had no pin before. Restored: blob 4170445f equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty; unablated: 18 passed.

objectql tests import source, so no dist rebuild leg was needed.
</details>

<details><summary>Gates</summary>

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at 4cc3e8b5 derived 69 families; 67 ran with exit 0 (`check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` first answered exit 3 on the shallow clone; its pinned fixture commit was fetched and it re-ran exit 0). `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exit 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: packages with no `dist/` in this tree) and `check:dts-closure` exit 1 (50 packages built without declarations in this shared tree) read the local build state, not this diff: NOT MEASURED locally, read from CI. `--ran` reconciliation: 69 derived, 68 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
</details>
